```text
In this house, magic is as ordinary as laundry, but only when you’re polite to the dust.
  The afternoon smells like lemon polish, warm cookies, and a little ozone, the scent of small spells.
    Lily appears at the top of the stairs, apron on, badge on, and a sparkly wand-pencil in her hand.
      “Rai,” she says, in the voice she uses when she’s about to be bossy. “I need help training.”
        “I have a babysitting certificate at school, and they said we have to practice with a baby.”
          She tilts her head, cheeks puffed with mischief.
            “I know a magic that can make you six for one evening.”
              “Your clothes will get loose, your knees will get smaller, your voice will get squeaky, but your thoughts stay yours.”
                “If you want the magic to feel more baby-like or less, you can say so.”
                  “Mom said you can’t be forced to be a practice baby, so I ask properly.”
                    “Will you let me turn you into my practice baby for the evening?”
                      “You control every word and action. I only get to play the bossy big sister.”
                        “What does Rai say or do?”
```
